```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE
)

# Load the data
music_data <- read.csv("data.csv")

# Show success message
cat("✓ SUCCESS! Loaded", nrow(music_data), "rows and", ncol(music_data), "columns\n")
cat("✓ Columns:", paste(colnames(music_data), collapse=", "), "\n")

# Keep only the 12 required columns
required_cols <- c(
  "acousticness", "artists", "danceability", "energy", "id",
  "liveness", "loudness", "name", "popularity", "speechiness",
  "tempo", "valence"
)

music_data <- music_data[, required_cols]

cat("✓ Now have", nrow(music_data), "rows and", ncol(music_data), "columns\n")

# Summary statistics
summary_stats <- summary(
  music_data[, c("danceability", "energy", "popularity", "loudness")]
)
print(summary_stats)

# Missing values check
missing_counts <- colSums(is.na(music_data))
print(missing_counts)

# Plot 1: Danceability histogram
hist(
  music_data$danceability,
  main = "Danceability Distribution",
  xlab = "Danceability Score",
  ylab = "Number of Tracks",
  col = "lightblue",
  border = "black"
)

# Plot 2: Energy vs Popularity scatter
plot(
  music_data$energy,
  music_data$popularity,
  main = "Energy vs Popularity",
  xlab = "Energy",
  ylab = "Popularity",
  pch = 19,
  col = "darkred",
  cex = 0.6
)

# Plot 3: Top 10 artists
artist_counts <- head(
  sort(table(music_data$artists), decreasing = TRUE),
  10
)

barplot(
  artist_counts,
  main = "Top 10 Artists by Track Count",
  las = 2,
  col = "steelblue"
)
